newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel reporter travelled to Syria with Chirac.
newsitem.headline: Israel reporter travelled to Syria with Chirac.

text.p: An Israeli reporter officially representing the Jerusalem Post newspaper was allowed to visit Syria during French President Jacques Chirac's weekend visit to Damascus, French officials said on Monday.
Eldad Beck, who travelled on an Austrian passport which shows he was born in Israel, was a member of the press party which accompanied Chirac.
French officials said Chirac's office had intervened with the Syrian authorities to win approval to take him along as a goodwill gesture in the stalled Middle East peace process.
Chirac personally asked Beck not to file any reports until they had left Damascus to avoid upsetting President Hafez al-Assad.

Beck told Reuters he was officially authorised to interview the head of the small remaining Jewish community in Syria, Youssef Jajati, but was not allowed to ask a question at a joint Chirac-Assad news conference on Sunday.

"I was allowed to travel freely during the trip and meet the Jewish community. The head of the community was officially authorised to speak to me to show the Jews of Syria are happy and well treated," Beck said.
Israeli reporters with foreign passports have visited Damascus on at least two previous occasions, but usually accredited for non-Israeli publications.

Jerusalem Post diplomatic correspondent David Makovsky said he had visited Damascus four times accompanying senior U.S. officials in 1994 and 1995, at a time when Israel and Syria were holding U.S.-brokered peace talks, which were broken off early this year.
He said his visit were made possible by the intervention of U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher.
